ai_technology: CoxBoost gene selection and random survival forest (CDIS)

evidence.ai_role: Learned gene selection and survival-forest predictions define CDIS for risk and immune-state comparisons.
evidence.tested: Existing-cohort survival scoring; three validation cohorts also informed selection. Separate cell-line BAFF assays concern a candidate pathway.
evidence.unknown: Prospective clinical benefit and portable preprocessing/cutoffs remain unestablished. Cell-line effects are not patient therapeutic evidence.

organization: Jinan University; You Jiang Medical University for Nationalities

source_review.scope: Primary full Methods and Results: model selection, cohort C-indices, frozen-scaling/cutoff failure, single-cell inference and BAFF assays; validation 2 applies prognostic claim.

summary: CoxBoost plus a random survival forest produced a 16-gene DLBCL risk score after comparison of 101 model combinations. Reported validation C-indices were 0.613, 0.732 and 0.632, but those cohorts contributed to model selection. More strictly frozen preprocessing lowered discrimination to 0.547, 0.591 and 0.596; the training cutoff classified almost all external patients as high risk. Downstream transcriptomic analyses suggested a BAFF/APRIL pathway, with BAFF effects tested in cell lines. These findings establish neither clinical benefit nor a validated treatment mechanism, and the cell-line assays do not independently validate prognostic transport.
title: Learned lymphoma risk score shows retrospective associations and transport limits
